About

Genocide-Free Cyprus is a grassroots, people-led collective on the island. We came together in 2024, as people in Cyprus watched their own ports, bases and institutions become part of the machinery of genocide against Palestinians, and decided that silence was complicity. There is no leader to personify and no brand to protect: whoever shows up and does the work is the collective.

Our work stands on three legs. Political analysis: documented, evidence-based writing that names who is complicit and follows how the complicity works, from military logistics to fuel supply chains. Media: photography, video and social coverage of the movement on the streets of Cyprus, so that what happens here is seen here and abroad. And culture: art, music, banners and public events that make the movement impossible to ignore, because culture reaches the people who will never read a policy paper.

Why this site exists

Cyprus has been used — its ports, its bases, its infrastructure — in service of wars and blockades documented as genocide. This site exists to document that complicity, publish the evidence and argument behind our campaigns, and give people on the island and beyond a place to act, not only read.

What we fight for is larger than any single campaign. We demand accountability and justice: a fair society and a world in which Cyprus, and every state, contributes nothing to genocide, apartheid, occupation or oppression of any kind. That obligation does not stop at Gaza. It applies wherever power is used against the people it governs or displaces.

We hold that accountability is not a mood but a demand. Cyprus has obligations under the Genocide Convention, and so does every state that lets its territory, fuel and infrastructure service this war. We document, we name, and we push for consequences: legal, political, economic and cultural.

Campaign

Bases Off Cyprus

Against the use of the British sovereign bases on Cyprus by the UK and US militaries in support of Israel's war on Gaza.

Campaign

No Harbour for Genocide

Against US tankers like the Overseas Santorini and Overseas Sun Coast, carrying jet fuel from Texas toward Ashkelon, stopping for servicing at Limassol along the way. Our harbours are not a stopover for genocide.
